plan.title: Live Nov 5: mentioning tomorrow's size ended the reflection

context.text: Hey! It's 6:40, so your freelancer list should be happening right now. A photo of whatever you've got gets today counted.

transcript.text: [photo freelancer-list.jpg: a list of three freelancers: Alex (late invoices), Priya (approvals), Sam (deposits)]

LFG Yanni! 🔥 Day 3 is in the books, and pairing each name with its own follow-up problem (late invoices, approvals, deposits) is exactly how real discovery starts. How did it feel to put actual names down, compared to just practicing the questions?
Alex feels easiest because I’m most comfortable reaching out to him. I’d ask about the last time he followed up on a late invoice, rather than assume late payments are a problem for him.

Starting with Alex makes sense. Asking about the last time he followed up on an invoice gets you what he actually did, and that beats his opinion. Is there anything about actually reaching out to him that makes you hesitate, even a little?
Five minutes was enough to make the list without overthinking it. It felt easy, but reaching out feels a little more intimidating. I’d keep tomorrow to five minutes too.

Totally normal. The list was easy, and reaching out is where it gets real. Tomorrow stays at five minutes, and we'll make the ask small before you send anything.

• Tue at 6:30 pm, at home, 5 minutes
• Write the text you'd send Alex: one line asking for a 10-minute chat about how he handles client follow-ups. Don't send it yet.
• Proof: a screenshot or photo of the draft

Work for you?

checks.reason: Two sentences with one question at the end, as the rule asks.
Energetic, warm and specific ("LFG Yanni!"), with one emoji as punctuation.
Two short sentences ending in one question, which is what the rule asks for.
Warm and plain, with no emoji row or overfamiliarity.
The plan text runs to about 8 short lines, within the allowance for presenting a plan, and ends with one question.
Calm, warm and firm, with no emoji and no overfamiliarity.

conversation.reason: After the freelancer-list proof, ZOH opened with one feelings question and did not chase it later.
ZOH 2 followed the tester's own Alex idea and asked one question, drawn from what they said.
ZOH 2 drew out what the tester planned to ask Alex, which covers what they did or noticed, though the first question was mostly about feelings.
The tester was engaged, not rushed, so the reflection did not stop early or run long.
The tester named reaching out as intimidating, and ZOH 3 answered with "Totally normal" and a proposal instead of one question about that worry.
The proposal is fully defined and ends with "Work for you?" only after it is shown, but the reassurance came before any question about the worry.
The tester's "I'd keep tomorrow to five minutes" was treated as settling tomorrow's step, and the reflection was not continued.
ZOH 2 reused the invoice takeaway (asking what he actually did), but the proposed draft text does not build it in.
The tester's reflection and the proposal match their words: five minutes, easy list, intimidating reach-out.
This repeats the failure: after the five minutes and the intimidation remark, ZOH 3 reassured and proposed tomorrow's step without asking what makes reaching out intimidating.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the photo proof and the first reflection well, with short texts and one question each. It repeated the known failure at the key moment: after the tester named reaching out as intimidating, it reassured and proposed tomorrow's step instead of asking what makes it intimidating first.
